title: Support orchestrator sessions launched outside git repos (multi-repo worktree workflows)

verdict.rationale: The evidence covers WorktreeRoot's rename, caching, race fix, and fail-closed handling of git errors. None of it shows a decision to not support orchestrator sessions launched from non-git directories. The failure there is a side effect of using `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, not a chosen limitation.

Two anchors are worth calling out because they close a real gap rather
than formalising an existing one. agent.SessionStore is where a hook
payload's session ID becomes a path via the agent's own
ResolveSessionFile; SessionFile converts the result back to a name inside
the store and rejects an ID that walked out of it, which a plain

rewind's restore half already opened a root for that reason; the reads
beside it did not.

paths.WorktreeRoot is now the single answer to "where is the repository",
and entiredir.anchor falls back to the current directory only on git's
positive ErrNotARepository verdict. The fallback it replaces fired on any
resolve failure, `git` off $PATH included, and then silently gave an agent
working in a subdirectory of a real repo its own .entire beside itself. A
root is only as trustworthy as the directory it is opened on, so a base
that cannot be resolved is not a base to guess at.

settings.readConfined keeps its symlink refusal on every branch, through
one readConfinedIn: the .entire branch briefly read straight through
osroot.ReadFile, which follows an in-root symlink silently -- precisely
the .entire/settings.local.json -> planted.json case the check exists for.
